calc.sip.title: SIP Calculator
calc.sip.desc: See what a fixed monthly investment could grow into over time.
calc.sip.explain.1: Each instalment is invested at the start of the month and compounds monthly at the expected rate, so early instalments do the heaviest lifting.
calc.sip.explain.2: The expected return is an assumption, not a promise. Market-linked investments can and do return less, including less than you put in.
calc.sip.faq.1.a: No. It is the rate you assume for the projection. Actual returns depend on how the underlying investments perform.
calc.sip.faq.2.q: What happens if I stop paying midway?
calc.sip.faq.2.a: Contributions stop but the balance stays invested and keeps compounding. Re-run the calculator with the number of years you actually contributed to see the difference.
calc.emi.title: Loan EMI Calculator
calc.emi.desc: Work out the monthly payment, total interest and payoff schedule for a loan.
calc.emi.explain.1: The payment is level for the whole term. Early payments are mostly interest; the share going to principal grows every month.
calc.emi.explain.2: Fees, insurance and any rate reset during the term are not included. A floating-rate loan will differ once the rate moves.
calc.emi.faq.1.q: Does paying extra reduce the interest?
calc.emi.faq.1.a: Yes. Anything paid above the scheduled amount goes straight to the principal, which cuts both the balance and all the interest that would have accrued on it.
calc.emi.faq.2.q: Why does the interest barely fall in the first years?
calc.emi.faq.2.a: Interest is charged on the outstanding balance, which is at its highest at the start. The breakdown table shows the crossover year for your figures.
calc.income-tax.title: Income Tax Calculator
calc.income-tax.desc: Estimate the tax on your annual income and what you keep after it.
calc.income-tax.hint.deductions.in: Section 80C, 80D, home loan interest and the rest, combined.
calc.income-tax.hint.deductions.us: Itemised deductions. They replace the standard deduction only if they exceed it.
calc.income-tax.hint.deductions.gb: Pension contributions and other allowable deductions.
calc.income-tax.status.head: Head of household
calc.income-tax.note.in: Salaried figures for FY 2025-26, including the standard deduction, the Section 87A rebate and 4% cess.
calc.income-tax.note.us: Federal tax and FICA for 2025. State and local taxes are not included.
calc.income-tax.note.gb: England, Wales and Northern Ireland for 2025/26, including Class 1 National Insurance. Scotland uses different bands.
calc.income-tax.note.ae: The UAE charges no personal income tax on salary income, so take-home pay equals gross pay.
calc.income-tax.explain.1: Income is reduced by the allowances and deductions you qualify for, then the remainder is taxed slab by slab - each rate applies only to the income inside its own band.
calc.income-tax.explain.2: The effective rate is total tax over gross income. The marginal rate is what the next unit of income would be taxed at.
calc.income-tax.faq.1.q: Why is my effective rate lower than my slab rate?
calc.income-tax.faq.1.a: Because only the income above each threshold is taxed at that slab's rate. The income below it is taxed at the lower rates, so the average always lands under the top rate you reach.
calc.income-tax.faq.2.a: No. This covers the main allowances and the standard deduction. Special reliefs, credits and local taxes are not modelled, so treat the result as an estimate.
calc.gst.title: {tax} Calculator
calc.gst.desc: Add or remove {tax} from any amount and see the split.
calc.gst.note.in: Within a state GST splits equally into CGST and SGST; across states the same total is charged as IGST.
calc.gst.note.us: Sales tax rates are set by state, county and city, so pick the rate that applies where the sale happens.
calc.gst.note.generic: {tax} is charged at the standard rate unless the goods or services fall under a reduced or zero rate.
calc.gst.explain.1: On a tax-exclusive amount the tax is added on top. On a tax-inclusive amount it is worked back out, which is why dividing by the rate is not the same as multiplying by it.
calc.gst.faq.1.q: How do I get the pre-tax price from a final price?
calc.gst.faq.1.a: Switch the amount type to "Tax already included". The calculator divides by one plus the rate, which is the only correct way to reverse it.
